rules.title: Legacy (non SDK-style) project format
rules.recommendation: Convert to SDK-style .csproj (manually or with the try-convert / Copilot modernization tooling). Remove explicit <Compile> items and AssemblyInfo duplicates.

rules.title: packages.config is used
rules.recommendation: Migrate to <PackageReference> (Visual Studio: right-click packages.config > Migrate packages.config to PackageReference).

rules.title: Targets .NET Framework
rules.recommendation: Retarget to net10.0 (or multi-target netstandard2.0;net48 for shared libraries during a gradual migration).

rules.title: ASP.NET (System.Web) web application project
rules.recommendation: Create a new ASP.NET Core host. For large apps consider incremental migration: YARP proxy in front plus System.Web adapters, moving endpoints one by one.

rules.title: WCF service application project
rules.recommendation: Host services in ASP.NET Core with CoreWCF (closest to existing code) or redesign as gRPC / REST APIs.

rules.title: ASP.NET Web Forms pages/controls
rules.recommendation: Web Forms are not available on modern .NET. Rewrite to Razor Pages / Blazor, or keep them on .NET Framework behind YARP while the rest migrates.

rules.title: Global.asax application events
rules.recommendation: Move Application_Start logic to Program.cs and per-request events (BeginRequest/EndRequest/Error) to middleware.

rules.title: HTTP modules (IHttpModule)
rules.recommendation: Rewrite as ASP.NET Core middleware.

rules.title: HTTP handlers (IHttpHandler / .ashx)
rules.recommendation: Rewrite as minimal API endpoints or middleware.

rules.title: ASP.NET session state
rules.recommendation: Use ASP.NET Core ISession (async, byte[]/string only, requires explicit serialization) backed by a distributed cache; review what is stored in session.

rules.title: Dependency on System.Web namespace
rules.recommendation: Replace System.Web types with ASP.NET Core equivalents (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http). Note: System.Web.HttpUtility is still available on modern .NET.

rules.title: ASP.NET Web API 2 (System.Web.Http)
rules.recommendation: Port controllers to ASP.NET Core: ApiController -> ControllerBase + [ApiController], IHttpActionResult -> IActionResult, HttpConfiguration/routes -> Program.cs, filters -> ASP.NET Core filters.

rules.title: ASP.NET MVC 5 (System.Web.Mvc)
rules.recommendation: Port to ASP.NET Core MVC: controllers, filters, bundling, Razor views (HTML helpers, @Html.Action -> view components).

rules.title: Static HttpContext.Current access
rules.recommendation: Inject IHttpContextAccessor (or pass HttpContext explicitly). Look for usages in non-web layers: they indicate layering problems that must be untangled first.

rules.title: OWIN / Katana pipeline
rules.recommendation: Replace OWIN middleware and Startup with the ASP.NET Core pipeline; Microsoft.Owin.Security.* -> ASP.NET Core authentication handlers.

rules.title: ASMX web services
rules.recommendation: ASMX is not supported. Replace with CoreWCF (SOAP compatibility) or REST/gRPC endpoints.

rules.title: WCF .svc service endpoints
rules.recommendation: Host with CoreWCF in ASP.NET Core (keeps contracts and SOAP clients working) or migrate to gRPC/REST.

rules.title: WCF server configuration (system.serviceModel/services)
rules.recommendation: Move bindings/behaviors to code-based configuration in CoreWCF; check that every binding used is supported by CoreWCF.

rules.title: WCF client configuration (system.serviceModel/client)
rules.recommendation: Modern .NET WCF client (System.ServiceModel.Http/NetTcp packages) does not read config files: move endpoints/bindings to code and appsettings.json.

rules.title: WCF service contracts ([ServiceContract])
rules.recommendation: Contracts can be reused with CoreWCF; for gRPC convert to .proto. Server-side contracts drive most of the WCF migration effort.

rules.title: WCF client proxies (ClientBase<T> / ChannelFactory<T>)
rules.recommendation: Client side is supported on modern .NET via System.ServiceModel.* packages; regenerate proxies with dotnet-svcutil and configure bindings in code.

rules.title: Self-hosted WCF (ServiceHost)
rules.recommendation: Replace ServiceHost with CoreWCF hosted in ASP.NET Core / Generic Host.

rules.title: .NET Remoting
rules.recommendation: Remoting is not supported. Replace with gRPC, HTTP APIs, or named pipes / StreamJsonRpc for IPC.

rules.title: AppDomain creation
rules.recommendation: Modern .NET has a single AppDomain. Use AssemblyLoadContext for plugin isolation/unloading or separate processes for security isolation.

rules.title: BinaryFormatter serialization
rules.recommendation: BinaryFormatter is removed from modern .NET (throws since .NET 9). Switch to System.Text.Json, MessagePack or protobuf and plan data migration for persisted payloads.

rules.title: System.Drawing usage
rules.recommendation: System.Drawing.Common is Windows-only on modern .NET. Fine if you stay on Windows; for Linux/containers use ImageSharp or SkiaSharp.

rules.title: Windows Registry access
rules.recommendation: Works on Windows only. Prefer configuration (appsettings / environment variables) if the target is containers/Linux.

rules.title: COM+ / System.EnterpriseServices
rules.recommendation: Not supported on modern .NET. Replace distributed transactions / serviced components with explicit transaction handling or messaging.

rules.title: ConfigurationManager usage
rules.recommendation: Works via the System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager package, but prefer IConfiguration / IOptions<T> with appsettings.json.

rules.title: Entity Framework EDMX model
rules.recommendation: EF Core has no EDMX. Reverse-engineer with Scaffold-DbContext, or keep EF6 (6.3+) with a code-first model; the EF6 designer does not work in SDK-style projects.

rules.title: T4 text templates
rules.recommendation: T4 is not run by dotnet build. Commit generated code or switch to source generators.

rules.title: Entity Framework 6 (System.Data.Entity)
rules.recommendation: EF6 6.3+ runs on modern .NET (lowest-risk first step). Migrating to EF Core is a separate effort: query translation, lazy loading and configuration differ.

rules.title: Custom configuration sections
rules.recommendation: Move to appsettings.json bound with IOptions<T>.

rules.title: Package must be replaced
rules.recommendation: Replace with the modern equivalent listed in the finding.

rules.title: Package must be upgraded
rules.recommendation: Upgrade to a version that supports modern .NET (see finding).

rules.title: Package not needed on modern .NET
rules.recommendation: Remove the package; the functionality is built into the SDK/runtime.

rules.title: Package compatibility unknown
rules.recommendation: Compatibility could not be determined (offline mode, lookup failure or missing metadata). Check the package's supported frameworks manually.

rules.title: Package incompatible with modern .NET
rules.recommendation: No supported version exists. Find an alternative or isolate the dependency behind an interface.

rules.title: Package works but is deprecated / needs review
rules.recommendation: Package runs on modern .NET but a newer recommended library exists; plan the replacement separately.

rules.title: Package not found on configured feeds
rules.recommendation: Usually an internal package: add its feed with --nuget-source, or plan to multi-target it (netstandard2.0;net48) before migrating consumers.
